raw_response:
I've been doing this for fifty years. I know this land. I know what works here in Quzhou, and I follow what has worked for my family and my neighbors.

My 8.7 mu will run the same rotation I always do — winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same ground after the wheat comes off in June. That's just how it's done here on the North China Plain. Both crops use all my land, one after the other.

**For the wheat:** I'll plant in early October, after I turn the soil with the rotary machine — I don't plough deep anymore, my back won't allow it, and rotary is fine. I'll use the improved wheat seed from the village supply store, the kind most people around here use. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then top up with urea in spring when the plants start pushing again. I water four times: once before winter sets in to help the roots, once in early spring, once at jointing, and once when it heads out. Powdery mildew and aphids are my main worries, so I spray twice. Expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if spring rains cooperate.

**For the maize:** Right after wheat harvest I direct-seed the maize — no tillage needed, the ground is already worked from wheat. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the supply station has that year, same as everyone. I put down fertilizer at planting and top-dress again at the big bell stage when the plant is growing fast. I irrigate at planting to get good germination and again around silking time if the sky is dry. I spray once for pests if I see armyworm or corn borer. Should get around 550 jin per mu.

Two of us eat from this farm. We sell the surplus. This plan feeds us and gives us something to sell at harvest.
